high.title: Stock Investors "Holding Breath" Before New Variable
high.summary: If at the beginning of 2026, the market was still debating how many times the Fed would cut rates, now the question has shifted to whether the Fed will have to raise rates again by year-end. The night of June 5 witnessed a widespread "risk-off" state when US stocks, Bitcoin, oil, and gold all fell sharply, while the USD and US government bond yields surged. This is the market's reaction to the scenario that the Fed may maintain high interest rates longer than expected, or even raise rates again. For Vietnamese markets, this creates significant headwinds as higher US rates typically strengthen the USD, potentially pressuring the VND and reducing capital flows to emerging markets like Vietnam. The risk-off sentiment could also impact Vietnamese equities through reduced foreign investment appetite and broader risk asset sell-offs.

high.title: Vietcap Presents 2 Scenarios for VN-Index in June, Names Stocks with Positive Prospects
high.summary: Vietcap assesses that the market is currently balancing between supportive factors in valuation and positive international context, while still facing pressure from foreign outflows and domestic macro concerns. Supporting factors include major regional and global stock markets continuing their upward trend, led by technology, semiconductor and AI infrastructure stocks. MSCI indices for emerging and developed markets rose 24.8% and 9.8% respectively in May, establishing new historical peaks. Vietnamese market valuation has become more attractive after the correction phase, with VN-Index trading at 15.3x P/E at end-May, below the 10-year median. Excluding VIC, VHM and VRE impact, the P/E drops to around 13x. This presents potential opportunities for tactical allocation, though foreign selling pressure and global monetary policy uncertainty remain key risks to monitor.

high.title: Vietnam Stock Market: What's Next After the Nearly 50-Point "Free Fall" Session?
high.summary: Vietnamese stock market started the week negatively, with VN-Index falling nearly 50 points to around 1,790 points on June 8. This was the deepest decline since late March, bringing the main index to its lowest level in nearly 2 months. Despite significant price discounts after the correction, bottom-fishing funds remained cautious, with liquidity not surging during the plunge at only around VND 16,000 billion, showing investor sentiment still leaning toward defense rather than aggressive buying. The sharp decline reflects global risk-off sentiment amid concerns the Fed may maintain high rates longer or even raise them again. For VND and bond markets, continued foreign outflows and risk aversion could pressure the currency and push investors toward defensive positions. Market participants should monitor upcoming Fed communications and domestic policy responses.

medium.title: Gold's Plunge: When Will It Stop?
medium.summary: Gold price developments over the past two decades show that strong upward phases are usually followed by significant correction periods. From the September 2022 bottom, gold entered a strong rally, reaching an all-time high of 5,594.82 USD/ounce on January 29. Since then, gold has declined about 20% to close at 4,473.8 USD/ounce. The larger the increase, the deeper the subsequent correction tends to be.

medium.title: Loss Amount for Those Who Bought Gold on Than Tai Day
medium.summary: Gold prices continued declining on June 8, with major brands quoting gold at 138.8 million VND/tael buying and 143.6 million VND/tael selling. Compared to Than Tai Day (February 26) prices of 184 million VND/tael selling, buyers face losses of 45.2 million VND/tael. The article advises against selling based solely on short-term price movements.

medium.title: VN-Index "Evaporated" Nearly 50 Points, Investors Await Extremely Important Event Next Week
medium.summary: VN-Index experienced its sharpest decline in nearly 3 months, losing nearly 50 points and breaking through 1,800 points. The sell-off occurred amid widespread "risk-off" sentiment globally, with increasing investor concerns that the Fed may maintain high interest rates longer than expected or even raise rates again. The VIX volatility index surged, indicating heightened market anxiety.

medium.title: Dr. Le Xuan Nghia: A Portion of People's Deposits Are Shifting Away from Banking System Due to Low Interest Rates, Tightened Tax Management and Asset Declaration
medium.summary: Former Deputy Chairman of the National Financial Supervisory Committee notes that the real estate market will continue to be supported by large capital flows in the economy, though facing challenges in mobilizing resources for growth. Some deposits are moving away from the banking system due to low interest rates and stricter tax and asset declaration management.

medium.title: Series of Board Members at One Bank Request Resignation
medium.summary: Eximbank received resignation requests from board members Pham Tuan Anh, Nguyen Tri Trung, and Nguyen Trong Hien ahead of the extraordinary shareholders' meeting scheduled for July 24, 2026. The meeting will consider board and supervisory board personnel matters. Chairwoman Pham Thi Huyen Trang will continue until the extraordinary meeting is held.
